prediction_ref.short_label: Agentic vulnerability scanning ships at a second major vendor by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
Direct origin evidence. Microsoft announced on July 9 that MDASH — its multi-model harness orchestrating more than 100 specialized AI agents to discover, debate, and prove exploitable bugs — is moving onto dedicated cloud infrastructure sized for Windows-scale scanning, the first production-scale operationalization of agentic vulnerability discovery by an OS vendor. The harness has already surfaced 16 vulnerabilities across the networking and authentication stack, including four critical remote-code-execution flaws in the kernel TCP/IP stack and the IKEv2 service, and Microsoft is publicly arguing calendar-bound patch cycles must give way to continuous, risk-driven remediation.
The agentic-scanning-at-a-second-vendor prediction is that by Q1 2027 another major OS or hyperscale cloud vendor announces its own production agentic scanning harness for a flagship codebase, with disclosed CVE counts and at least one program tying findings to off-calendar risk-driven patching. Today supplies the first-mover instance, the symmetric-threat framing that pressures peers, and the commodity orchestration ingredients (GPT-5.6 ultra mode, Muse Spark tool-use) that make replication cheap; the second vendor announcement is what remains.
